newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada sees positive 1997 economic outlook.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada sees positive 1997 economic outlook.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said the outlook for Canada's economy in 1997 remained favorable, despite uncertainties about output in the fourth quarter this year, according to the minutes of a Bank of Canada board of directors meeting released on Wednesday.

In remarks to the October 17 meeting Thiessen said there were signs that economic activity had picked up in the third quarter of this year as rising consumer confidence and past reductions in interest rates led to increased housing activity and retail sales.

But the governor noted that prospects for the fourth quarter were more uncertain due to "recent volatility in employment data" and a strike at the General Motors Corp's Canadian subsidiary in October.
He said Canada's inflation was likely to remain in the lower half of the Bank's 1.0 to 3.0 percent target range in "the period ahead."

Thiessen also said that Canada's improved fiscal performance, low inflation and improving economic fundamentals have resulted in rising investor confidence in the country's financial markets and a firmer Canadian dollar.

"As financial markets increasingly focused on Canada's low inflation, the improvement in public finances and the swing into surplus of the balance of international payments, the Canadian dollar has appreciated and interest rates have declined for all terms of maturity," the Bank's minutes said.
